content.rationale:
tqxvykwn accepts that the graph can reference an id no document carries and asks the viewer to show that condition rather than hide it; U1 makes activation a route into the one selection a canvas click already makes (ltrnmrsr), with a single selected node and a single detail render, so the panel cannot describe one node while the canvas emphasises another. This decision fills the case U1 explicitly left open — a listed id that names no node document — with the only outcome consistent with both: the entry stays listed, and activating it leaves the selection and the panel where they are.


Inert beats the two alternatives. Selecting nothing and blanking the panel would have to invent a selection target that has no node and no detail: the panel would go blank at the moment the reader is reading the selected node's section, so the reader would lose the panel's view of the node they were learning about precisely because they tried to follow one of its recorded relationships, and the viewer would gain a second notion of selection — a selected id with no node behind it — which is the drift U1's single-selection rule exists to prevent. Reporting an error is no better: a dangling reference is a fact the graph records, not a failure of the interaction, so an activation error would make an ordinary recorded state look like a viewer fault, would make a click in the panel read as a fault, and would contradict the shape U1 gives activation — one select-and-show-detail outcome, not a place where warnings surface. Nothing happened because there was nothing to select, and saying nothing — selection unchanged, detail unchanged — is the accurate account of it.


Dropping the entry instead would be worse than either, because it would hide the condition. rmovtvkt has each section list the edges the node records, and mkyoyqvt makes a depends_on or evaluates edge a real edge whether or not its other end resolves, so the selected node's declaration would vanish from the panel while tqxvykwn still marks that edge on the canvas — two accounts of the same node disagreeing about what it records. Listing the inert entry keeps one account: the same missing id is marked where the edge is drawn and listed where the node's relationships are reported.


That is also why the panel half belongs here rather than to tqxvykwn or to the rendering. This node states a behaviour — activation has no effect — for an id the panel already has, adds no appearance and no canvas rule, and leaves the drawing of the sections to the composition (tpztomkv) and the styling of the entry to the stylesheet decisions. U1 and tqxvykwn are the settled edges it builds on, not rules it repeats.
content.content:
An id listed in one of the detail panel's four relationship sections (rmovtvkt) is listed but inert when the other end of the edge it comes from names no node document, and this decision is about that id alone. The case it covers is the selected node's own field naming an id that no node document carries — a depends_on or evaluates edge the selected node declares whose other end is missing — which is the dependency or evaluation tqxvykwn records as referencing a missing node id. The reverse sections are not that case: "dependents" and "evaluators" list the documents that declare the edge toward the selected node, so those listed ids name a node, and U1 (kwxutvpw) settles activation for them unchanged. Only this unresolved case is settled here: an id that reaches the viewer by some other route is not an entry in one of these four sections, and this decision states nothing about it.


The entry stays an entry. It is not hidden, omitted from its section, filtered out, dropped from the section's list, merged with a neighbour or replaced by stand-in text, a warning or an empty state; it keeps its place among its sibling ids in its section, in the labelled frame rmovtvkt and vqwoptmu fixed. The panel therefore still reports the edge the graph records from the selected node to that id, listed exactly as its sibling entries are listed, rather than turning a recorded edge into an absence.


Activating it changes nothing. U1 settles activation for an id that names a node the panel has and leaves the id that names none unstated, which is the id this decision settles. A listed id takes the two inputs U1 fixed — a pointer click, and Enter or Space while the entry has focus — and on an id that names no node document neither of them changes the viewer. The selection stays where it was: the node whose section the entry sits in remains the selected node, and nothing is selected in its place — not the missing id, not a neighbour, not an empty selection. The detail panel keeps showing that node's detail as it was showing it, unblanked, with no error, message or empty state standing in for it. The two inputs are not two outcomes here: a click and Enter or Space do the same thing, which is nothing.


None of this is a statement about appearance. No class, style rule, hover cue or focus cue is added to the entry by this decision: it keeps the plain id look its sibling entries have, and whether it is styled, or given a focus indicator, is left to the stylesheet and presentation decisions that own appearance, as U1 left it. Nor does this decision restate, replace or extend tqxvykwn's marking. That decision requires the viewer to render the edge as unresolved and mark it visibly on the canvas, and this one leaves that requirement in force: the missing node document is one recorded condition with two presentations — the edge marked visible on the canvas (tqxvykwn) and the id listed but inert in the panel, each the same condition seen where the reader is looking. The panel entry carries no mark of its own because the mark tqxvykwn requires is the edge's; the canvas marking needs nothing from the panel, and the panel needs no mark from the canvas.


Out of scope, each owned elsewhere and said once: what the canvas draws for the unresolved edge is tqxvykwn's and is not decided, narrowed or repeated here; reveal-into-view is not settled here; opening the node document is not settled here, and an id that names no document has none to open; a double-click variant is not settled here, activation being U1's pointer click and Enter or Space only; and what activating an entry that names the node already selected does is not settled here. In must-not terms, the viewer must not hide or drop the entry, must not report its activation as an error or a fault, must not change the selected node or the detail panel when the entry is activated, and must not put another node in the missing id's place.
